items.summary_1line: Long-context applications, long-lived agents, and multi-agent systems require large language models (LLMs) to process and retain extensive information. In these settings, the KV cache can exceed GPU high-bandwidth mem...

items.title: BridgeKV: Large-Model Prefill and Small-Model Decoding for LLM Inference via KV Cache Translation
items.summary_1line: LLM inference has two phases with different bottlenecks: LLM prefill runs once per request and is compute-intensive. Decoding repeats for every output token and is limited by memory bandwidth. To address the challenge...

items.title: RoCoKV: Accelerating LLM Inference Serving through Uncertainty and Redundancy Aware KV Cache Compression
items.summary_1line: KV cache compression is critical for large reasoning models, where most of the cost comes from long generated reasoning traces rather than the input prompt. These traces often contain redundant and low-utility tokens...
items.editor_note: KV compression aimed at long reasoning traces, pruning redundant, low-utility generated tokens.

items.title: TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer-Wise Streaming
items.summary_1line: TideCache is a serving system for hybrid LLMs on CPU-GPU superchips that reallocates GPU memory among cache types and streams KV prefixes layer by layer, implemented in SGLang and tested on GB300 and GH200.
items.editor_note: Hybrid-attention cache management on CPU-GPU superchips, implemented in SGLang and tested on GB300 and GH200.

items.title: Abstract What Varies, Reuse Longer Patterns: Efficient Offline Chain-of-Thought Compression
items.summary_1line: CRAFT is an offline method that abstracts problem-specific details into slots, compresses shared expression templates once, and applies the edits to build shorter chain-of-thought training targets, cutting compressor budget by a median 90.7%.
items.editor_note: Output-side reduction: builds shorter chain-of-thought training targets, cutting compressor budget by a median 90.7%.

items.title: LoomKV: Lossless KV Cache Compression from GPU Memory to SSD for LLM Serving
items.summary_1line: LoomKV is a lossless KV cache compression system for LLM serving that works on an unmodified engine, storing BF16 KV at 0.71 of raw size and reporting 2.7-3.6x raw goodput on the AgentX trace across LMCache's LRU cliff.
items.editor_note: Latest item: first lossless, engine-unmodified KV compression in the thread, with goodput numbers against LMCache.

editorial.tldr: This is a theme thread, not one event: 13 items from Nov 6 to Nov 24 that each cut LLM serving cost at a different layer, mostly arXiv papers plus Google's XLA Serving Engine launch and an AWS case study. Through Nov 19 the KV cache was the most-attacked target, ending with RoCoKV and TideCache.
editorial.whats_new: LoomKV (Nov 24) compresses the KV cache losslessly from GPU memory down to SSD on an unmodified serving engine, storing BF16 KV at 0.71x raw size and reporting 2.7-3.6x raw goodput on the AgentX trace.
editorial.why_it_matters: KV-cache memory is the dominant serving bottleneck in this thread (7 of 13 items), and LoomKV is the first entry that claims lossless savings without engine changes, so cache tiering may become a drop-in layer rather than a fork.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you offload KV cache with LMCache or similar, measure goodput as the working set crosses your LRU capacity before adding GPUs; that cliff is where LoomKV claims its gains.
